title: A person's deliberate block on u9h was silently dropped by the run's own merge, which keeps dispatching the attempts the block exists to stop (fourth counterexample)
body: At 18:41:09 local the session lead committed 1b725f49 (origin/main): tick 37i created and "37i" added to u9h's blocked_by, so the run 'stops cycling on it and stops spending interventions'. At 18:43:32 the run's merge 96977e99 (origin/main into epic/dha) resolved .tick/issues/u9h.json byte-identical to the run side, deleting the "37i" entry; the claim and the tick-graph read that admitted u9h both happened before the merge, so the block was never visible to the orchestrator, which dispatched attempts 22, 23, 24 AND 25 against the person's recorded intent — four counterexamples, each one spending the go6 interventions the block exists to prevent, with attempt 24's report explicitly saying 'do not dispatch attempt 25' before this dispatch. The shape: a file the run rewrites (.tick/issues/<tick>.json) receives a human edit on main, and the run's merge resolution takes its own side verbatim, so any person's governance edit to a live tick is silently reverted while a run is mid-claim; the reconciler's tick-graph read must happen after the main merge and before dispatch, and a merge that drops a blocked_by entry added by a non-run author must fail loudly rather than resolve. Still unfixed and still untriaged at attempt 25.
